run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T08:14:19Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by a dependency failure below frontend, not by frontend itself: from the 08:14:19Z sample onward frontend's own spans for cart/checkout calls carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, the cart service's own server spans for GetCart/AddItem also carry STATUS_CODE_ERROR, and the cart pod's logs switch at 08:13:21Z from clean operation to repeated Redis connection failures. The Redis backend valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is Running but not ready, restartCount 4, last termination OOMKilled exit 137 at 08:17:18Z, state CrashLoopBackOff, with a 10Mi memory limit and no probes; the pod cgroup max usage reached exactly 10485760 bytes at the 08:14:19Z sample. The valkey-cart Service has only notReadyAddresses, and valkey BackOff events run 08:14:17Z-08:21:35Z, matching the alert start 08:14:19Z. Pre-incident traces at 07:49:59Z show the same cart->redis path succeeding, so this is new in the window. frontend, cart and frontend-proxy pods are ready with 0 restarts, and product-catalog/ad/recommendation/payment/accounting error series stayed at zero. The exact alert expression, valkey's own logs/metrics and change history could not be obtained; the remaining sub-question (what pushed valkey memory to its limit) stays a hypothesis.

claims.text: frontend's own spans begin carrying STATUS_CODE_ERROR at the 08:14:19Z sample and were zero at every earlier sample from 07:50:19Z: GET /api/cart 0.13978695238095237/s at 08:23:19Z, POST /api/cart 0.37083333333333335/s at 08:21:19Z, executing api route (pages) /api/cart 0.5/s at 08:21:19Z, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.24583333333333332/s, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem 0.25416666666666665/s, POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder also nonzero; frontend's GET /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations error series stayed at 0 for the whole window.

The cart service's own server spans error in the same period: span_name POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem reaches 0.2583333333333333/s and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.26666666666666666/s at the 08:21:19Z sample, with first nonzero values at 08:15:19Z in the 5-minute rate; cart span POST /oteldemo.CartService/EmptyCart stays near 0.

checkout shows its own error spans in the window (oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.086339/s and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 0.056161/s at the 08:23:19Z sample, HTTP POST 0.05416666666666667/s), and frontend-proxy shows ingress error spans rising to 1.1916666666666667/s at 08:21:19Z with router frontend egress 0.1625/s.

cart's pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 logs its first Redis connectivity failure of the window at 2026-11-15T08:13:21Z ("Connection failed. Disposing the object", then "Error status code '{StatusCode}' with detail '{Detail}' raised.", then "Connection to redis was restored successfully." at 08:13:31Z and "Successfully connected to Redis" at 08:13:36Z); no redis/connection error line exists in that pod's logs between 07:50:00Z and 08:13:21Z.

The same cart pod continues flapping against Redis: 08:14:16Z "Connection failed. Disposing the object", 08:14:24Z "Wasn't able to connect to redis", 08:14:35Z "Successfully connected to Redis", then from 08:15:15Z repeated "Connection failed"/"Wasn't able to connect to redis"; the newest 60 matching lines (08:20:38Z-08:21:42Z) are an unbroken stream of "Wasn't able to connect to redis" plus the error-status line.

valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft is Running but not ready: Ready=False reason ContainersNotReady message "containers with unready status: [valkey-cart]"; container valkey-cart has restartCount 4, state waiting reason CrashLoopBackOff ("back-off 1m20s restarting failed container=valkey-cart"), lastState terminated reason OOMKilled exitCode 137 startedAt 08:17:07Z finishedAt 08:17:18Z; container is image valkey/valkey:8.1.3-alpine with requests cpu 2m/memory 4Mi, limits cpu 10m/memory 10Mi, livenessProbe null and readinessProbe null; owner is ReplicaSet valkey-cart-58df56c79c.

Kubernetes events for valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft show 22 Warning BackOff occurrences "Back-off restarting failed container valkey-cart" spanning firstTimestamp 2026-11-15T08:14:17Z to lastTimestamp 2026-11-15T08:21:35Z, plus 6 Normal Created and 6 Normal Started events between 07:36:47Z and 08:18:53Z for the same pod.

Deployment valkey-cart has spec.replicas 1 with availableReplicas null, readyReplicas null and unavailableReplicas 1, and its Service Endpoints object contains only a notReadyAddresses entry (100.96.5.138:6379, targetRef pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft), i.e. no ready Redis backend behind the valkey-cart service; cart's Deployment by contrast is 1/1 available and ready.

cAdvisor memory series for pod valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft show the pod cgroup max usage stepping from about 5.8 MB (5836800 bytes at 08:12:19Z) to exactly 10485760 bytes (10Mi, the container memory limit) at the 08:14:19Z sample and 10493952 bytes at 08:18:19Z, while the valkey-cart container working-set samples were only about 3.5-4.3 MB and several distinct container IDs appear between the 08:14:19Z and 08:20:19Z samples, consistent with repeated container restarts.

Pre-incident behaviour was healthy: traces of service cart in 07:14:19Z-07:50:00Z (data ending 07:49:59Z) show POST /oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and POST /oteldemo.CartService/GetCart spans with Redis child spans HMSET/HGET/EXPIRE completing, and frontend's POST /api/cart plus frontend-proxy ingress spans carrying http.status_code="200" and grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem with rpc.grpc.status_code="0"; no error rows in that sample.

frontend, cart and frontend-proxy pods are all Running/ready with restartCount 0, so the alerting frontend container never restarted; all otel-demo pods including valkey-cart were created around 07:36:39Z, and valkey-cart kept the same pod name valkey-cart-58df56c79c-4cvft and same owner ReplicaSet across its 4 restarts, so the crash-loop is in-place container restarts, not a new-pod rollout at incident time.

Parallel dependencies were not failing at the same time: frontend's client spans to product-catalog (grpc.oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct), ad (grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds) and recommendation (grpc.oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations) read 0 error rate at every sample; payment's GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect and accounting's "orders receive" error series read 0 at every sample; frontend's tcp.connect error series read 0.

Most likely causal chain: the valkey-cart container repeatedly exceeds its 10Mi memory limit (pod cgroup max usage touching 10485760 bytes at the 08:14:19Z sample) and is OOM-killed (last termination OOMKilled, exit 137 at 08:17:18Z), leaving the single-replica Redis deployment with no ready endpoint and entering CrashLoopBackOff; cart then intermittently cannot reach Redis and returns gRPC errors on GetCart/AddItem, which frontend surfaces as error spans on /api/cart and /api/checkout, matching the frontend RequestErrorRate alert. The 08:13:21Z first cart Redis failure, 08:14:17Z first valkey BackOff event, 08:14:19Z first frontend/cart error-span sample and the alert's own 08:14:19Z start are consistent in time.

Open sub-question attached to the same entity, not a second cause: what drove valkey-cart memory from about 5.8 MB toward its 10Mi limit at about 08:14Z (workload/data growth versus an out-of-band configuration change) cannot be determined from the available evidence, since valkey-internal metrics and change history were unavailable.

Rejected: a frontend application defect as the origin. frontend's error spans are confined to cart/checkout callspans (grpc.oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, grpc.oteldemo.CartService/AddItem, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout) while its product-catalog, ad and recommendation client spans stayed at zero errors, its pod is ready with 0 restarts, and the first backend (cart-to-redis) failure at 08:13:21Z precedes frontend's first nonzero error sample at 08:14:19Z.

Rejected: cart's own deployment or pod failing. Deployment cart is 1/1 available and ready, pod cart-755465879b-4p8d9 is Running ready with 0 restarts, and its error output names the Redis connection ("Wasn't able to connect to redis", "Connection failed. Disposing the object") with recovery lines ("Connection to redis was restored successfully") that track valkey-cart's crash/restart cycle.

Raise the valkey-cart container's memory request/limit (currently requests 4Mi, limits 10Mi) to a value that leaves headroom for valkey's real working set, and add a readinessProbe and livenessProbe on port 6379 so the pod leaves Service endpoints deliberately and recovers cleanly instead of crash-looping; verify whether a configuration change introduced the 10Mi limit.

Add dependency-health alerting for the cart path (valkey-cart readiness/restart count and cart-to-redis connection errors) so the OOM crash-loop itself pages instead of only the downstream frontend request-error rate, and monitor valkey memory against its limit.

gaps: The alerting rule could not be read: list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned status no_data (no rules), so the exact expression and metric behind RequestErrorRate and the reported value 3.0222222222222217 were not reproduced or verified.

No trace-level evidence of the failure: traces_search for service cart in 08:10:00Z-08:33:19Z returned status no_data, and traces_search_by_tags error=true for service frontend returned status no_data; the usable trace sample ends about 07:50Z, so failure-window spans are unknown and the window's error evidence comes from span metrics, which count spans (internal, client and server) rather than requests.

The first traces_search for service frontend in 07:14:19Z-08:33:19Z returned RESULT_TOO_LARGE with status error and is not citable; its rows were not read, so that sampled span view remains unexamined.

valkey-cart container logs are unavailable: fetch_pod_logs returned status no_data with 0 lines for the current instance and no previous instance (previous container not found), so valkey's own OOM/startup messages could not be read.
frontend pod logs are unavailable: two fetch_pod_logs reads of frontend-675fd7b5c5-x9gbm returned status no_data with 0 bytes read, so frontend-side log errors could not be confirmed or excluded.

No http_server_request_duration_seconds_count series exists on this target (get_all_labels returned status no_data), so the alert's underlying request-level metric was not found by that name and no request-denominator could be computed.

No valkey/redis internal metrics (memory usage, evictions, persistence) exist in this Prometheus target, and cAdvisor samples are 30s-2min apart, so what pushed memory to the 10Mi limit at about 08:14Z and the exact peak cannot be established.

Change history integration is not available (not_integrated: change_history), so whether valkey-cart's memory limit/requests or probes changed shortly before 08:14Z is unknown; no new ReplicaSet or pod was observed, but config changes cannot be ruled in or out.
Metric and trace data end before the query window end (span-metric source_end_at 08:26:19Z and 08:25:19Z, trace data about 07:50Z), so the final minutes of the window are not covered.

Not checked to conclusion: email, currency, quote, image-provider, kafka and shipping services produced no error-span series in the per-service query, which is an unknown rather than evidence of health for them.
next_steps: Read the RequestErrorRate alerting rule and its expression from the Prometheus rule configuration to confirm which metric produces the 3.02 value and whether it is a per-second or per-window rate.

Inspect valkey-cart memory behaviour at scrape resolution (or add valkey INFO metrics) and review whether the 10Mi limit and 4Mi request come from the Helm values; raise the limit and add readiness/liveness probes on 6379 under a change request.
Review the cart service's Redis client retry/timeout and error handling so single-replica Redis restarts do not immediately surface as errors on /api/cart and /api/checkout.
Verify whether a configuration rollout or Helm values change preceded 08:14Z once change history is available.
